stem:
\(\frac{12x + 28}{4} - \frac{s}{13} = r(x - 8)\)
In the given equation, s and r are constants, and s > 0. If the equation has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of s?
solution_steps: Simplify the left side: (12x + 28)/4 = 3x + 7, so the equation becomes 3x + 7 − s/13 = r(x − 8)
Expand the right side: 3x + 7 − s/13 = rx − 8r
For infinitely many solutions, coefficients of x must match: r = 3
why_this_difficulty: Hard: requires simplifying a compound fraction, then applying two simultaneous conditions for infinitely many solutions — coefficient match and constant match.
